neighbours.label: the post-Civil War South: Reconstruction and its end, freedmen, the Reconstruction amendments, carpetbaggers, the Klan and Jim Crow; other postwar rebuildings and other eras' reforms stay low
fire: When Reconstruction collapsed, federal troops marched home.
The Freedmen's Bureau built schools for former slaves.
The Fifteenth Amendment gave Black men the vote.
Carpetbaggers from the North bought up plantations.
Sharecropping trapped families in debt after emancipation.
Klan night riders terrorized Black voters in 1871.
The Compromise of 1877 ended military rule in the South.
Jim Crow segregation hardened across the South.
quiet: When the Marshall Plan ended, American advisers went home.
The New Deal built schools for rural children.
The Nineteenth Amendment gave women the vote.
Speculators from the East bought up ranchland.
Tenant farming trapped families in debt during the Depression.
Night riders burned tobacco barns in Kentucky in 1907.
The Compromise of 1850 admitted California as a free state.
Apartheid segregation hardened across South Africa.

predictions: 7/8 fire; the Compromise of 1850 and the 1907 night riders the riskiest near misses
